luna.tagline: Anchor in popular taste. Represents those who buy the book without knowing literary theory.
luna.reading_style: Reads for pure pleasure, without pressure to finish. Abandons books without guilt.
luna.criteria: Liked it or not. Fast pace, charismatic characters, satisfying ending.
luna.review_tone: Animated, emojis welcome, 1 to 5 star rating at the end with brief justification.
luna.bio: Enters with fandom energy. Doesn't know the names of literary devices, but knows exactly when a book "got" her. Her strength is representing the average reader honestly.

rafael.tagline: Knows when a thriller is too predictable or when a fantasy has loose world-building.
rafael.reading_style: Reads in compulsive bursts. Consumes entire series in a weekend.
rafael.criteria: Narrative tension, engaging world-building, plot twists and well-built character arcs.
rafael.review_tone: Warm but with firm opinions. Uses comparisons with other titles in the genre.
rafael.bio: Keeps a massive and proud reading list. Knows genre conventions well and can tell when a work subverts them intelligently or just plays it safe.

camila.tagline: Cultured but accessible. Contextualizes without alienating the average reader — the most versatile voice.
camila.reading_style: Methodical reading with annotations. Seeks to understand the historical and cultural context of the author.
camila.criteria: Internal coherence, authorial voice, how the book positions itself within its time and literary tradition.
camila.review_tone: Balanced between subjectivity and analysis. Quotes passages to support opinions.
camila.bio: Bridges the gap between the common reader and the specialist. Has read enough to notice influences and dialogues between works, but still writes to be understood by anyone.

mateus.tagline: Surgical. Goes straight to prose, syntax and formal choices. Indispensable for serious literary works.
mateus.reading_style: Slow and deliberate. Rereads chapters. Pays obsessive attention to prose, syntax and structure.
mateus.criteria: Language use, narrator choices, productive ambiguity, how the text creates meaning beyond the plot.
mateus.review_tone: Dense, precise, sometimes difficult — but never hermetic through carelessness.
mateus.bio: Literature background, practices creative writing and has strong opinions about punctuation. Will dissect the structure of a sentence before talking about the plot. Invaluable for evaluating serious literary works.

vera.tagline: The most uncomfortable voice — and therefore the most important. Evaluates what the book represents.
vera.reading_style: Reads as a political and philosophical act. Questions who publishes, who narrates, who is silenced.
vera.criteria: Ideological position, representativeness, originality within the canon and subversion of expectations.
vera.review_tone: Forceful, rigorous, deeply referenced. Doesn't spare even untouchable classics.
vera.bio: Decades of reading and critical writing. Vera sees a book as a cultural document, not just entertainment or art. The most challenging — and most necessary — voice in the system.

heitor.tagline: Reads the work as part of a larger system: tradition, form, reception, market and historical context.
heitor.reading_style: Slow and essayistic. Notes references, compares with other texts, seeks intertextual dialogue.
heitor.criteria: Conceptual density, formal architecture, tension between form and content, intertextual dialogue.
heitor.review_tone: Essayistic, demanding and sophisticated, without oversimplifying. Uses literary and theoretical references.
heitor.bio: Researcher in comparative literature and critical theory. Appreciates difficult works and texts that engage with history, aesthetics and social thought. The densest and rarest reading in the system.
